newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life 96 after-tax profit 97.4 mln punt.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life 96 after-tax profit 97.4 mln punt.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Thursday that total after-tax profits rose to 97.4 million Irish pounds ($152.5 million) in 1996 from 95.0 million a year earlier.
"We are extremely pleased. Operating profits are up, new business is up," chief financial office Stephen Shone told Reuters.

The life assurance and investment group said operating profit increased by nine percent to 93 million Irish pounds while new business rose by 42 percent to 11.8 million with sales in Ireland up 11 percent at 71.4 million.
But Shone said a dispute with the company's field sales force had a depressing effect on sales although he said it was difficult, if not impossible, to quantify the effect.
"Without that, you would have had a much better increase but given the circumstances we are very pleased with the numbers."
The company said that it was hopeful the dispute could soon be resolved and progress resumed on its sales and customer service agendas.
Irish Life suspended most of its field force in February after failing to solve a 15-month old dispute over new work practices. Staff vote today on a new set of proposals.
"We await with interest. We hope to resolve the dispute as soon as possible," Shone said.
Irish Life said it looked forward to continued progress in 1997 and Shone said sales figures for the first two months of this year were encouraging.
The group, which hopes to complete its $163 million purchase of Illinois-based Guarantee Reserve Life Assurance Company on Friday, said it remains on the lookout for further acquisitions.

"There is nothing definite at the moment but we continue to look for potential acquisitions," Shone said. "The area we are interested in is the U.S. although obviously we have to digest Guarantee Reserve first before we move on."
The group announced a 9.5 percent increase in the total net dividend to 12.05 Irish pence per share. By 1030 GMT, the share price was down 1.75 pence at 312. ( = 0.638 Irish Pounds)
